column1: # v15_bounds against v12_pairs, plus the two Stage 0b brackets.
# Asking two things in one batch.
# 1. Does removing the three bounds-checked loads pay, when it is done without changing the
#    loop's shape? v13 removed the same checks (and the table header reloads) via `first_chunk`
#    returning Option and `probe_words` returning false, both of which add exits from the hot
#    loop, and lost 15 ms. v15 removes only the checks, through raw-pointer windows feeding the
#    same `_win` functions v13 added. Disassembly: the interleaved loop goes 214 -> 203
#    instructions per two rows; 28 check instructions leave and the register allocator puts 19
#    back as rematerialised constants.
#    Both thread counts, because the optimum stream count already differs between the core
#    tiers and instruction count should matter more on the narrow ones.
# 2. What is the ~24 ms `v12_pairs` spends outside `main`? `null` is exec + dyld + runtime
#    setup + teardown with no work; `spawn` adds 18 threads that set their QoS and return.
# Each binary is entered twice under two labels. Those pairs are the batch's noise floor and
# nothing smaller than their spread may be read as a result.
